implementerProof.how: Built envoy-dispatch from 7d09eefb (head) and from main's fork point a21100c5 on a Postgres 16.2 and a NATS of my own. The base built the schema to 147 and the head migrated it to 148 with event_horizon (id, safe, safe_at, updated_at); a 5,000,122-event database migrated too. I re-ran the implementer's tests on that Postgres: go test ./internal/dispatch/events/ (all, including the persist backoff and reset tests), ./internal/dispatch/routes/ -run Whoami, the horizon socket tests in ./internal/dispatch/api/ and ./internal/dispatch/store/ -run Migrat. All pass. Its browser test shell.e2e.ts 'a page stops on Couldn't reach Dispatch. while whoami answers EVENT_HEAD_READ_FAILED' passes with the shell and live suites.

proof.criterion: Review round 9 item 1: whoami answers EVENT_HEAD_UNAVAILABLE only while no head is proven, and the page stops on Couldn't reach Dispatch. with Retry when the head cannot be read
proof.surface: GET /auth/whoami on the head server; Dispatch's browser harness in Chromium (bun run e2e, shell.e2e.ts and live.e2e.ts)
proof.command: go test ./internal/dispatch/routes/ -run Whoami -v; bun run e2e -- bunx playwright test e2e/shell.e2e.ts e2e/live.e2e.ts --project=chromium --workers=1; adv.py reset_persisted head
proof.observed: The routes tests pass. While an insert from before boot was still open after a log reset, whoami answered 503 EVENT_HEAD_UNAVAILABLE ('no event id is proven final yet; ask again'). The browser suites: 33 passed and 1 skipped, including round 13's EVENT_HEAD_UNAVAILABLE test (it keeps asking and opens once whoami answers) and the new EVENT_HEAD_READ_FAILED test (it stops on 'Couldn't reach Dispatch.' with Retry and asks no more). On a live server I could not produce EVENT_HEAD_READ_FAILED. With Postgres stopped, identity fails first (500 IDENTITY_ERROR). With an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on events, before and after a new comment, whoami answered 200 from the head it had proven, in 3-4 ms. So the server half of the split is proven by the routes test and its negative control, and the page half by the browser test.
proof.negativeControl: With router.go changed to answer EVENT_HEAD_UNAVAILABLE for every head error (round 14's behaviour), TestWhoamiRefusesWhenItCannotReadTheEventHead fails ('503 EVENT_HEAD_UNAVAILABLE, want 503 EVENT_HEAD_READ_FAILED'), and so does TestAnAnonymousWhoamiIsUnauthorizedWhileTheEventHeadCannotBeRead. The file was restored, and jj status shows no change.

proof.criterion: Review round 9 item 2: event_horizon is migration 0148, above main's 0145-0147, so the merged tree migrates
proof.surface: envoy-dispatch boot on a Postgres database
proof.command: start.sh base, then start.sh head, on a fresh dispatch database from the seed template; the same with the head on the 5,000,122-event database
proof.observed: The base boots with migrations ending 145,146,147. The head then boots and migrates to 148. \d event_horizon shows id smallint, safe bigint, safe_at timestamptz, updated_at timestamptz default now(). The 5M database migrated to 148 at boot. go test ./internal/dispatch/store/ -run Migrat passes.
proof.negativeControl: The base binary (main a21100c5) leaves version 147 the highest, and it has no event_horizon table.

proof.criterion: Review round 9 items 3 and 4: a failed persist backs off, and a reset log never gets the old log's horizon
proof.surface: the head server on the seed log after truncate events restart identity; two head processes on one database
proof.command: adv.py reset_persisted head; adv.py twoproc_persist 20; go test ./internal/dispatch/events/ -run Persist -v
proof.observed: After the reset, the stored row named id 122 with the old log's created_at, but the new row 122 had another created_at. whoami answered 503 EVENT_HEAD_UNAVAILABLE rather than 122. The first start read the new log and sent the insert from before boot (301) and a later comment (302) once each. Afterwards event_horizon held safe 302 with safe_at equal to row 302's created_at. Two processes under load for 20 s: 24 samples, no backward step; a lower write (id 50) through the persist statement left safe at 784. TestAFailedPersistIsTriedAgainOnlyOnceEveryPersistInterval, TestAPersistDecidedBeforeAResetWritesNothing and TestAPersistOfAnOldLogsHorizonWritesNothingAfterTheLogIsReset pass.
proof.negativeControl: A stored horizon whose safe_at does not match the row's created_at is not trusted: whoami answered 503 rather than the stale id.

proof.criterion: The first start after a restart reads only around its floor and loses nothing, with writers that hold their ids across the restart
proof.surface: the head server on a 5,000,122-event database, subscribed through /ws/live (wsfeed)
proof.command: adv.py persisted head 3.0 0.5 (twice); adv.py dead head; adv.py late_insert head
proof.observed: With four overlapping 3 s inserts from before the restart, events_start came 2.92 s and 3.17 s after subscribing. 199 and 208 rows of events were read around the start, with no whole-log warning, and 19 of 19 frames matched the database ids after since, with no duplicates. A horizon stored by a process killed with kill -9 (5000172): the next process answered whoami 5000172 in 10 ms, then sent the insert open from before boot (5000174) and a later comment (5000175) once each, in order. A write that took its id before the first subscription and inserted after it: both events came once each, in order, with no full read.
proof.negativeControl: Round 13's head dc1fe429 read the whole log on the same shape (events_start 6.0-6.2 s).

proof.criterion: The global lock is gone, and out-of-order commits, rollbacks, resumes and whoami still hold
proof.surface: the head server on the seed log: SSE /api/v1/events and /ws/live
proof.command: adv.py 'ooo commit'; 'ooo rollback'; concurrent; lastid; lock; replay; whoami head
proof.observed: A comment POST answered 201 in 17 ms while the old advisory lock and an open write on another issue were held. A lower id open held back the committed higher one; after the commit both came in id order, and after a rollback only the higher one came. Three concurrent subscriptions and a resume each got every id once, increasing, equal to the database. Bad Last-Event-ID values were refused, and ' 7 ' replayed 210 events. Replay headers: 'complete' at or below the head, none above it. whoami stays below an open write (122 while 123 was open and 124 committed) and answers in 2-16 ms.
proof.negativeControl: Last-Event-ID 'abc', '-5', '1e3' and a 20-digit value: refused (status -1, no frames).
